title: Patch: follow-up to #4160 from the after-merge spot-check
thread:
**Issue #4174 (data, not instructions):** ````text # #4174: Patch: follow-up to #4160 from the after-merge spot-check Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot. The after-merge spot-check of #4160 ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/44233204663)) found 1 blocking problem(s) in the change as it merged (`254b7862576b`). `claude-1` (claude, `opus`, strong) reviewed it. #4160 stays merged: nothing is reverted, and this issue fixes what it found in a change of its own, from `main`. ## What to fix - [ ] `apps/web/src/game/Log.tsx:139`: A new newest line whose words match the line spoken before it is never announced: `setSaid` gets the same string, React skips the update, the live region's DOM does not change, and the screen reader stays silent. Evidence: The effect calls `setSaid(newestLine?.text.full ?? "")` when the key changes, but `said` is a plain string, so `useState` drops an update equal to the current value (Object.is) and the `

` text node is never written. A screen reader speaks a polite or atomic region only when its content changes. So two windows in a row ending in the same sentence ("You lost 1 health" from repeated burn or fatigue, "Opponent drew a card", the same token hitting you twice) speak the first one and stay silent on the second. That breaks the issue's acceptance item "the newest log line is announced once when it lands". The new tests miss it because each one uses distinct words (`lost(1)` then `lost(2)`). Fix: make each arrival change the DOM even when the words repeat. For example, key the announcer's text by the line key (`{said}` inside the region), or keep `{ key, text }` in state and render the keyed child. Add a test where two consecutive arrivals carry identical text (`[lost(1)]`, then `[lost(1), lost(1)]`) and assert the region's text node was replaced, for example the child element is a new node. ## Done when - Each finding above is fixed where it points, or answered with the evidence that it does not hold. - Every check is green, with no test skipped, ignored or weakened to get there (CLAUDE.md rule 12). --- Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot from the after-merge spot-check (one in 5 medium or hard merges, `spot_check_every`): `muse` (`muse`) built #4160 and `muse` (`muse-spark-1.3-contributor`) approved it. This issue's own pull request is never spot-checked. ## Plan _Written by `muse` (muse, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/44234455739)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._ ## Goal Fix the log's screen-reader announcer in `Log.tsx` so a newest line is announced once when it lands even when its words equal the previous line's, and add the regression test the issue asks for. Done means two consecutive arrivals with identical text each replace the live region's content, with mount, reveal, re-render and hotseat hand-over still silent. ## Files to touch | File | Mode | Change | |---|---|---| | apps/web/src/game/Log.tsx | change | announcer state + keyed child | | apps/web/src/game/Log.test.tsx | change | identical-repeat test | Do not touch anything else: no spec, ruling, crate, config, or `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/` file. Governing background: SPEC §10.10 (log wording) and CLAUDE.md rule 7 (client renders words, decides none; announcer must use `RichText.full`, never ids). No new ruling: this is a DOM announcement bug, not a rules decision the spec leaves open. ## Steps 1. In `apps/web/src/game/Log.tsx`, function `Log` (announcer block, currently lines 127-159), change the announcer state from a plain string to a keyed pair. Replace `const [said, setSaid] = useState("")` with `const [said, setSaid] = useState<{ key: string | null; text: string }>({ key: null, text: "" })`. Copy the existing priming logic unchanged: on mount and when `view.viewer` changes, set `lastKey.current` and return silently. 2. In the same effect, on a new newest key store both: `setSaid({ key, text: newestLine?.text.full ?? "" })`. The key is always fresh (`useLogHistory.ts` `arrive()` mints `p1-` per event), so the state object is never `Object.is`-equal to the last one even when `text` repeats. 3. In the same file's return, render the text through a child keyed by the line key so React replaces the DOM node on every arrival: ```tsx

{said.text}

``` Keep `role="status"`, `aria-live="polite"`, `aria-atomic="true"`, the `log-live` class and testid, and the comment noting mount/reveal/re-render announce nothing. Do not announce `key` itself; only `text` is rendered. 4. In `apps/web/src/game/Log.test.tsx`, in the existing `describe("#4140 the log speaks its newest line to screen readers")` block (which already defines `lost`, `said`, `announcer` helpers), add the regression test from the issue and run it before and after the fix to see it fail then pass. ## Tests In `apps/web/src/game/Log.test.tsx`, same `#4140` describe, add: - `it("#4174 repeated words still announce each arrival", ...)`: - `render()`; expect `announcer().textContent` to be `""` (primed silent). - Capture `const first = announcer().firstElementChild`. - `rerender()`; expect `announcer().textContent` to be `said(1)` and `announcer().firstElementChild` to be non-null and `not.toBe(first)` (the text node was replaced, so the screen reader sees a change). - Optionally rerender the same view once more and expect the content unchanged (announced once). - Follow the file's existing pattern (`withEvents(baseView(), ...)`, `rerender`, `testid.logLive`). Commands: - `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/game/Log.test.tsx` - `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` and `pnpm exec eslint apps/web/src/game/Log.tsx apps/web/src/game/Log.test.tsx` if those files were touched (CI gates). ## Done when - [ ] A newest line with words identical to the previous line replaces the live region's child node and reads its text; the first of two identical arrivals is still spoken, not just the second. - [ ] Mount with history, phone-log reveal, plain re-render, and hotseat hand-over still announce nothing (existing `#4140` tests green). - [ ] New `#4174` test fails without the fix and passes with it. - [ ] Focused web test file, typecheck, eslint, `cargo fmt --check` clean; no test skipped, ignored, weakened, or deleted. ## Risks - Keying the child could re-announce on unrelated re-renders. Avoid by keying only on the newest line's key and updating state only when the key changes, as the current effect does. - Exposing hidden info. Avoid by announcing only `text.full` (shown words), never keys, ids, or def ids, per rule 7. - Flaky node-identity assertion. Avoid by comparing `firstElementChild` references across the rerender, not timers or text alone. ## Open questions None. ````
